key_insight: The paper argues that Hyperball-style optimizers are not automatically a "free lunch": their apparent gains depend on the geometry of parameter updates, not just norm control. The authors introduce an angular effective learning rate that better explains optimization behavior by combining parameter angle, parameter norm, and update norm.
problem_solved: It addresses the open question of why Hyperball optimizers work well for scale-invariant deep networks and whether their benefits come from a genuinely better learning dynamic or from a misleading norm-based interpretation of progress.
method: Derive an angular effective learning rate based on the angular displacement between consecutive parameter states.
Incorporate three factors into the update analysis: parameter-update angle, parameter norm, and update norm.
Compare the new angle-aware measure against conventional norm-based measures to explain Hyperball-style behavior more accurately.
impact: For practitioners, this work provides a more faithful way to understand and tune optimizers for scale-invariant models. It suggests that controlling norms alone may not explain training success, so angle-aware diagnostics can lead to better optimizer design and more reliable training decisions.

paper_title: Hyperball May Not Be a Free Lunch
paper_authors: Yihao Xiao, Jialong Sun, Zitian Gao, Zeming Wei, Chutian Wang
